severity_criteria.source_excerpt: protocolSection.eligibilityModule.eligibilityCriteria: "* Patients need to have an IGA hand and foot score of 3 or 4 (moderate-to-severe disease) at screening and baseline" "IGA is an assessment scale used to determine severity of hand and foot AD and clinical response to treatment on a 5-point scale (0 = clear; 1 = almost clear; 2 = mild; 3 = moderate; 4 = severe) based on erythema and papulation/infiltration." -- Eligibility states hand/foot IGA 3 or 4 at screening and baseline; the registry outcome description supplies the 0–4 scale anchors.

prohibited_concomitant: Topical and systemic medications for treatment of atopic chronic hand and foot dermatitis during treatment period
permitted_concomitant: Low to medium potency TCS creams for AD on body areas other than hands and feet
value.population_note: SAP describes dupilumab monotherapy. It separately allows restricted low-to-medium potency topical corticosteroid creams for AD outside the hand/foot treatment area; rescue treatment on hands/feet is permitted when medically necessary.

background_therapy.source_excerpt: 2.1 Study Design and Randomization: "This is a phase 3, global, multicenter, randomized, double-blind, parallel-group, placebo-" "controlled study investigating the efficacy and safety of dupilumab monotherapy in adult and" "adolescent patients with moderate-to-severe atopic hand and foot dermatitis." "The use of topical and systemic medications for the treatment of atopic chronic hand and foot" "dermatitis will be prohibited during the treatment period." "However, patients will be allowed to use" "topical medications for AD on parts of the body other than hand and foot." "These topical" "medications will be limited to low to medium potency TCS creams." "If medically necessary (ie, to control disease" "flares), rescue treatment in the form of high potency TCS on hand/foot and/or systemic" "immunosuppressants may be provided to study patients at the discretion of the investigator." -- The explicit monotherapy description coexists with restricted topical use on other body areas and investigator-discretion rescue; prohibited/permitted lists preserve the anatomical and treatment-period limits.

multiplicity_control.source_excerpt: 5.6.3 Adjustment for Multiple Comparison; Table 1: "A hierarchical procedure, will be used to control the overall Type-1 error rate at 0.05 for the" "primary endpoint and the secondary endpoints of dupilumab versus placebo." "Each hypothesis will" "be formally tested only if the preceding one is significant at the 2-sided 0.05 significance level." "The hierarchical testing order is shown in below table (all comparisons are with the placebo)." "Table 1: The Hierarchical Testing Order" "Level Efficacy Endpoints (EPs) at Week 16 Testing" "Proportion of patients with IGA (hand and foot) 0 to 1 1" "Primary endpoint (on a 5-point scale)" "Key Secondary endpoints Proportion of patients with improvement (reduction) of 2" "weekly average of daily hand and foot peak Pruritus" "NRS ≥4" "Secondary endpoints Percent change in mTLSS for hand/foot lesions from 3" "baseline" "Percent change from baseline in weekly average of daily 4" "hand and foot peak pruritus NRS" "Change from baseline in weekly average of daily hand 5" "and foot peak Pain NRS" "Percent change from baseline in Hand Eczema Severity 6" "Index (HECSI) score" "Proportion of patients with HECSI-75 7" "Change from baseline in percent surface area of hand and 8" "foot involvement with AD" "Change from baseline in QOLHEQ 9" "Change from baseline in weekly average of daily Sleep 10" "NRS" -- SAP explicitly states hierarchical testing controls overall Type I error at 0.05 and tests each hypothesis only if the preceding one is significant at two-sided 0.05. value.source_inconsistency: The protocol calls study duration approximately 28 weeks excluding screening, while screening itself lasts 4 to 8 weeks; total_duration_weeks is therefore left null rather than treating 28 weeks as the whole trial.

study_schedule.source_excerpt: Sections 6 Study Design and Duration; 9.1 Schedule of Events and Table 1: "The study consists of 3 periods:" "• Screening period (minimum duration of 4 weeks and maximum up to 8 weeks)" "• Randomized treatment period (16 weeks)" "• Post treatment follow-up period (12 weeks)" "During the treatment period, patients will have in-clinic visits at week 2 and" "week 4, and then in-clinic visits every 4 weeks (Q4W) through week 16 with" "bi-weekly phone visits in between the in-clinic visits." "Patients and/or" "The end of treatment visit will occur at week 16, 2 weeks after the last dose" "The end of study visit will occur at week 28." "Study Duration The duration of the study for each patient is approximately 28 weeks," "• Proportion of patients achieving an IGA (hand and foot) score of 0 or 1 at week 16" "Table 1: Schedule of Events" "V1 V1a V2 V3 V4 PV51 V6 PV71 V8 PV91 V10 V11 Unsched ET visit" "In-Clinic Visit (V)* or uled" "Phone Visit (PV) visit2" "Week (W) W2 W4 W6 W8 W10 W12 W14 W16 W28" "Week (W) W2 W4 W6 W8 W10 W12 W14 W16 W28" -- The protocol gives screening as a variable 4 to 8 weeks; randomized treatment lasts 16 weeks and post-treatment follow-up lasts 12 weeks. Clinic visits are at weeks 2 and 4, then every 4 weeks through week 16, with intervening phone contacts. Phone weeks 6, 10, and 14 are the exact every-other-week contacts between the stated clinic weeks. Week 28 is the end-of-study visit. The endpoint criterion is the actual week 16 IGA 0 or 1 response, not the baseline eligibility score of 3 or 4.

value.applies_to_period: During the study; rescue for hand and foot disease is allowed after day 14.
value.rationale: Rescue for worsening hand and foot AD may be provided at investigator discretion after day 14, after an IGA assessment and only for IGA hand and foot score at least 3. Topical-first escalation after at least 7 days is encouraged only if possible, so no unconditional first_step or minimum-days rule is encoded. Patients may continue study treatment after topical or systemic rescue.

rescue_therapy.source_excerpt: Section 8.3 Rescue Treatment; Sections 8.4.2 and 11.4.3: "Rescue treatment for worsening of AD of hands and feet may be provided to study patients at the" "discretion of the investigator in the study." "14 of the study." "Investigators will be required to perform an IGA for hands and feet assessment" "prior to starting rescue treatment and initiate rescue treatment only in patients who have an IGA" "hand and foot score ≥3." "If possible, investigators are encouraged to consider rescue initially with" "adequately after at least 7 days of topical treatment." "treatment if rescue consists of topical medications." "Investigators can also use systemic corticosteroids or non-steroidal systemic immunosuppressive" "continue study treatment if rescue consists of these systemic therapies, based upon discretion of" "whether or not they complete study treatment and whether or not they receive rescue treatment for" "for all remaining study visits per the visit schedule." "Page 79 of 108" "CONFIDENTIAL" -- Day 14 is retained in applies_to_period because earliest_week is week-granularity. The IGA threshold is a required assessment before rescue; discretion remains the trigger. The topical-first sequence is qualified by 'if possible', so first_step and topical_min_days_before_systemic remain null. Continue-treatment and post-rescue responder handling are represented separately.
